Buried in it is the best thing on the page — Stockhausen answering a CD-R handed over in an autograph line with a letter warning him off sixths and kitsch, and a flat prediction that he would end up scoring films.

issues.forecast: The strongest work on the field this week is not a launch — it is a syllabus. A month-long architecture studio in Accra, a film festival in its fifty-second summer, a label naming its mill on the garment tag: the transmission systems are outperforming the drops, and the reveal cycle is the only place heat is still running ahead of the work.
come_up: Pedagogy as the venue — studios and festivals out-transmitting launches
Provenance named on the object — mill, weave and deadstock on the label
São Paulo bass exporting itself instead of being sampled
decline: Pre-alpha teasers spending attention a build has not earned
Summit-stage group shows curated around a diplomatic theme
The single-city scene report — the hybrids are already two continents deep
issues.climate: Teaching over launching — the field is rewarding the institutions that hand something down, and discounting the reveal that has nothing to hand over yet.

entries.name: Nomadic African Studio 2026 — The New Non-Aligned
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: The African Futures Institute moved its studio to Accra for four weeks and pointed it at the 1950s Non-Aligned Movement — not as nostalgia, but as a working question about what autonomy looks like against digital empires and extractive economies. The framing is the part that lands: not utopia, not collapse, but speculative survival — how housing, labour, energy and ecology get made liveable under pressure. Accra is the correct room for it. The city argued Pan-Africanism into being once already. Sitting through 14 August, and almost nobody outside architecture knows it is happening.

entries.name: Newark Black Film Festival — 52nd Edition
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive
entries.read: Fifty-two years. Screenings every Wednesday at the Newark Museum of Art, free, running to 5 August. The longest-running Black film festival in the country has been doing the work since 1974 with a committee of volunteers and museum staff picking the slate, and it still travels almost entirely by word of mouth in Essex County. That is the tell. Institutions this old usually calcify or get bought; this one just kept programming. Free admission is not a marketing choice here — it is the thesis.

entries.name: badsista
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy
entries.read: The São Paulo DJ and BANDIDA co-founder is the one Brazilian producers name when asked who moved trap-bass into techno without it reading as a costume change. She has worked with Linn da Quebrada and Kelela; her catalogue runs from ghetto-edit blends to the harder end of the club. São Paulo has been right about her for years — the gap is geographic, not qualitative. Baile funk is filling London rooms while most of the crowd cannot name a single producer, and she is the correction to that.

entries.name: AHABAN — Ajepomaa Design Gallery
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears
entries.read: Named for the Akan word for leaf. Handwoven Aso Oke, Fugu, organza and cotton batik cut from deadstock pulled out of GTP's mills in Accra — the material sourcing is not a sustainability footnote, it is the argument. Most houses working this lane say heritage and mean print. Ajepomaa names the weave, the mill and the origami pleating technique on the product page, which is the whole difference between a story and a receipt. Priced in cedis first, dollars second. That ordering matters.

entries.name: Project Override — Inuv8 Studios
entries.benchmark: Moonshots
entries.read: Ile-Ife is the right address for a game about a preservation unit waking up after 1,073 failed attempts to override the past — the Yoruba origin city building the archive-that-survives-collapse story is almost too neat. The ability framework, combat systems and narrative tooling are reportedly in. But this is a pre-alpha teaser with no platform, no window and an open call for publishers, and it has already collected more coverage than most shipped African titles get in a year. The lane is real. The read is early. Come back when there is a build.

issues.forecast: Three July releases, three running times: seven minutes out of Croydon on the 8th, twenty-seven out of Detroit on the 10th, seventy-eight out of a California state prison on the 17th. In the galleries the same arithmetic holds — ninety ceramics in Long Island City reading as a single argument, one beaded panel in San Francisco holding an entire migration. Compression is doing the work volume used to do. The long dump still charts; it just stopped meaning anything.
issues.climate: Compression over volume: the edit is where authorship now lives, and a release that refuses to end is telling on the room that let it run.
come_up: Fixed-length releases: 7 minutes, 27 minutes, no filler tax
Artist-owned imprints handling their own distribution — CHRRY, Street Certified
Hand-material archive work: raku clay, cowrie, Nymo thread
decline: The double album as proof of life
A chart debut mistaken for a verdict on the work
Weekly singles that exist to keep a catalogue warm

entries.name: Akinsanya Kambon — Soul Sessions
entries.benchmark: PanAfrica lane — Project a Black Planet. Kambon's ceramics are the kind of object that show exists to argue for; he sits level with it, not beneath it.
entries.read: The title comes from Vietnam. Kambon served with the Marines from 1966 to 1968 as an infantryman and combat illustrator, and the soul sessions were weekly gatherings Black Marines organised to teach each other. He has been running some version of them ever since. He came home, joined the Sacramento chapter of the Black Panther Party as Lieutenant of Culture, and did layout and illustration for The Black Panther. Then thirty years teaching art at Cal State Long Beach, plus free youth programmes out of his own studio. He is eighty. This is his first survey in New York. Over ninety figurative ceramics at SculptureCenter, made from the 1970s to now, fired in raku adapted with eucalyptus leaves and sawdust so the surfaces come out with a metallic sheen no kiln schedule can promise. The show is organised as seven sessions rather than seven decades: Thrones of Resistance, The Middle Passage, Rebellion and Uprising. Works on paper and archival material continue at CARA on West 13th, and the wall text tells you to take the E or F between the two. That instruction is the thesis. The room caught up in 2023 with the Hammer's Mohn Award; the work was finished long before the room arrived. Closes 16 August.

entries.name: Bandgang Masoe — M.O.N.E.Y.
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane — Chris Crack. Same instinct for the two-minute song as a finished thought rather than a sketch.
entries.read: Fourteen songs, twenty-seven minutes, forty-two seconds. Out 10 July on Street Certified Records, his third project of the year, and not one track overstays its welcome: Rent Due, Bread On My Mind, Don't Forget The Ricc, gone. Masoe has been in the BandGang orbit since the early-2010s Detroit run, and his most-played record is still Fuck a Baecation from 2018, a posse cut he shares with Babyface Ray, who left the lane and became a national name. Masoe stayed and kept the tempo. Twenty-two thousand monthly listeners against two million plays on an eight-year-old feature is the whole Detroit export economy in two numbers.

entries.name: Javan — Dare You/N2S
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane — Jim Legxacy. South London, diasporic, auteur R&B; Javan is a few years back down the same road.
entries.read: Javan has settled on a release shape almost nobody uses any more: a double A-side, no album, no rollout, one drop roughly every ten weeks. Dare You/N2S arrived 8 July on his own CHRRY imprint — three songs, seven minutes — his third of 2026 after One More Shot and FATAL ATTRACTION/MAGIC. He was seventeen when Mixtape Madness handed him a Next Up? in June 2019, out of Croydon, and the seven years since have gone entirely into singles with no full-length attempted. The Instagram reads nine and a half thousand followers, seventeen posts, and a bio that says Let God. The gap is that the release discipline is already professional while the audience is still village-sized.

entries.name: Demetri Broxton — Ancestral Echoes: Crops of Empire
entries.benchmark: heritage-craft lane — Dame Atlas, Tamera. The material discipline rhymes; the object is a wall, not a product.
entries.read: Japanese glass beads, sequins, cowrie shells, recycled glass, 24-karat gold-plated brass, rayon chainette, wool, Nymo thread, serigraph on Japanese sateen cotton, goat-hair canvas, birch board. That is the material list for one panel, 59 by 29 inches. Broxton works from family photographs whose subjects were never named, tracing the move from the American South out to Oakland, and beads the gaps rather than filling them. MoAD's Salon gallery, 685 Mission Street, through 16 August.

entries.name: Tory Lanez — Made You Think I Was Gone …But
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane — Starlito is the nearest thing on the 50, and it isn't close: comparable output, opposite relationship to editing.
entries.read: No interviews, no festival dates, no press run, no artist in the building. The tenth album still opened at No. 35 with roughly 19,700 first-week units, which is a real fact about how distribution works in 2026 and the most interesting thing on offer here. Everything after that is arithmetic: 23 tracks, 78 minutes, split into a rap disc and an R&B disc, his second album of the year, released 17 July on his own One Umbrella from the California Men's Colony, where he is serving ten years for shooting Megan Thee Stallion. Volume is the argument because volume is the only thing available. The 50 rewards taste over reach; this is reach with the taste removed.

issues.forecast: What failed this week was enforcement, not taste: eight trade bodies proposed an AI label for streaming and left compliance to whoever volunteers, while the work that held its shape arrived in small signed units — 96 pages from Penguin, a 12HP module with an open SDK, one drum pattern six years deep. Authorship over announcement.
issues.climate: Authorship over announcement. Every object that cleared the gate tonight names a person you could write a letter to: a Chicago poet, a São Paulo producer, a four-person module shop, a designer who cuts her own knots. The loudest item on the board names a committee, and the committee made compliance optional.
come_up: Open-SDK instruments — Hermetic Modular on the Electrosmith Daisy
Brazilian 2-step and brime — CESRV, Speedtest, 2 STEP MAFIA BRASIL
Poetry as a $20 object — Penguin Poets' summer list
decline: Voluntary industry standards — the eight-body AI label
The AI download as a product — TIDAL delisting, Udio's walled garden
Debut campaigns with no mill behind them

entries.name: Phillip B. Williams — Lift Every Voice
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: Ninety-six pages, twenty dollars, three hours read aloud by the author, out July 14 on Penguin Poets. Williams came up in Chicago, went through Cave Canem, and has spent a decade collecting the kind of prizes that usually pull a poet toward the lecture circuit: the Kate Tufts for Thief in the Interior, a Whiting, a Lambda, an American Book Award for Mutiny, then Ours in 2024, a novel-length act of conjure. Lift Every Voice goes the other way. It is short, and the compression is the achievement. The poems set a mother who knew seven ways to say one word under her breath against a grandmother whose smile reflects the world, then land on what Williams calls the impossible lift of forgiveness. Nobody scores a book of poems on volume, which is why it takes the cover: the object is small, priced for anybody, answerable to no committee, and it will outlast every product announced this month. Penguin already has it flagged a best seller in pre-order, so the room is arriving. It has not arrived. Get there before the syllabi do.

entries.name: CESRV — BRIME!! / FRONT 2 DA BACK
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy
entries.read: Brime was never a crossover. When CESRV pressed BRIME! to vinyl in 2020 with Febem and Fleezus — the first Brazilian grime record on wax — the sleeve carried the 2012 Club World Cup final, Corinthians over Chelsea, and the argument was settled in the image before a bar landed: São Paulo was taking London's 140 and keeping it. Six years and one sequel later (BRIME!!, six tracks, April 1, Beatwise / EMPIRE) he surfaces on the 2 STEP MAFIA BRASIL compilation with "FRONT 2 DA BACK," pointing the tamborzão at American garage instead. The scene he started is now big enough for outsiders to file reports on. He is still the one moving the reference.

entries.name: Torishéju — When It Rains, It Pours
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears
entries.read: Boiled wool and duchesse satin, tied and bound until the knot distorts the body underneath it. Torishéju Dumi has shown since 2023 on deadstock and a Yoruba reference chain, and her first fall campaign puts both on film, Sølve Sundsbø shooting, Ellie-Grace Cummings styling. Apple helped pay for it, which is where the honest note goes: a debut campaign is a marketing object, not a collection, and the coats and cardigans revisiting Yorubaland dress are the part still standing in five years. The room is right about her. It got there on the clothes rather than the credits.

entries.name: Alchemy Lab — Hermetic Modular
entries.benchmark: Koala Sampler
entries.read: Most build-your-own-module ambition dies at the breadboard. Alchemy Lab is 12HP around an Electrosmith Daisy — 480 MHz, 64 MB of SDRAM — with six CV jacks fully exposed to an open-source hardware abstraction layer, 102 addressable LEDs, and a delay launching beside it that stretches to sixteen seconds. The detail that decides it: no price, no ship date. Platform first, product later.

entries.name: The AI Label — Eight Bodies, One Suggestion
entries.benchmark: Leveraging AI
entries.read: On July 10 eight organisations — the RIAA, IFPI, the Recording Academy, SAG-AFTRA, A2IM, WIN, IMPALA and the Human Artistry Campaign — proposed two streaming tags, AI-GENERATED and AI-ASSISTED, modelled on the explicit-content marker. Five days later TIDAL stopped paying royalties on tracks it reads as fully synthetic. One of those is a rule. The other is a suggestion, written that way on purpose: platforms opt in. So the same file can earn full royalties on one service, get demoted on the second and disappear from the third without a note changing. Note what it isn't: a floor. The independent artist this is meant to protect still has no answer on Spotify, and this week a man was due in a New York court over eight million dollars of streaming fraud that ran seven years before anyone stopped it. The disclosure conversation is loud and it is correct. The enforcement is a press release.

issues.forecast: Cape Town, Warsaw, a stretch of coast west of Accra: the three strongest rooms this week are all run by people who declined to let the market set the terms, and the strongest of the three belongs to a painter who builds work he has no intention of selling. Inheritance over invention.
issues.climate: Inheritance over invention. Everything that cleared the gate this morning points backwards on purpose: a Xhosa proverb used as a working method, a Ghanaian textile school named after what hands remember, a Nigerian curator seating a Polish abstractionist beside Ndebele geometry and Xhosa clay, a novelist who recorded the audiobook with her own daughter. The one entry asking to be judged on its narrative rather than its record is also the one furthest down the board.
come_up: Material as argument — cow dung and raw pigment on unprimed Belgian linen
Craft schools over brand incubators — Kokrobitey's fourth intake, Aug 16
Estates handing the keys to outside curators — Gierowski Foundation, Warsaw
decline: The comeback narrative as the product — press cycle outrunning the record
Novelty as a curatorial default
African material culture priced as spectacle

entries.name: Mawande Ka Zenzile — Indlela Ibuzwa Kwabaphambili
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey
entries.read: A river that never dries up, is never celebrated is cow dung and oil stick on unprimed Belgian linen, and the material is the thesis rather than the texture. Ka Zenzile has painted with dung for over a decade; what has changed at Stevenson Cape Town, where the show runs 4 July to 15 August, is that he no longer uses it to argue against Western painting. He uses it as a knowledge system that was always sufficient on its own. He is also a practising traditional healer, and he describes the studio in those terms: incense, pipe smoke, music, the rational mind quieted until a colour flashes. His earlier paintings were representational and politically legible. These are intuitive, and harder to file. The detail that decides it: the show includes installations and interventions that cannot be bought, which he counts as artworks made for the audience's experience rather than for a wall. Inside a commercial gallery, inside a market that rewards African material as spectacle, that is a deliberate cost. Asked what he wants a visitor to leave with, he says art cannot be limited by what is fashionable. Fifteen August is the deadline and Cape Town is the only address.

entries.name: Valeria Luiselli — Beginning Middle End
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: Knopf published it on 28 July: 368 pages, thirty-five dollars, a mother and a teenage daughter driving Sicily after a divorce. The audiobook is the tell. Luiselli reads it across eight hours with Maia Enrigue Luiselli, her own daughter, which turns a decade of accusations about autofiction into a production credit. Four generations of women, a grandmother's archaeological dig, migrants met on the roadside: this is the Lost Children Archive method turned on her own family line instead of somebody else's border. Publishers Weekly starred it. The room is correct here, and it took the room four novels to get correct.

entries.name: Kokrobitey Institute — What Hands Remember
entries.benchmark: Material Culture
entries.read: The most useful institution in West African fashion this year is not a brand. It is a two-week workshop, 16 to 30 August, at an institute the artist Renée Neblett founded in 1992 on the coast west of Accra. The fourth edition is titled What Hands Remember, and the faculty is the whole argument: practising kente weavers and the textile scholar Seyram Agbleze sit alongside a Nigerian designer and the French designer Soline Charrier. Esi Otoo runs the Esi Sweater Project there, turning textile waste into handwoven garments and paid work for weaving communities. Earlier editions sent participants into Kantamanto market and the landfills behind it to source material. Curriculum, not campaign.

entries.name: Aether Commons — Azu Nwagbogu at the Gierowski Foundation
entries.benchmark: Project a Black Planet
entries.read: Warsaw is doing what Venice keeps announcing it will do. The Stefan Gierowski Foundation, set up in 2014 by the painter's family to look after his estate, handed the reinterpretation of that estate to Azu Nwagbogu, the Lagos curator behind LagosPhoto and the African Artists' Foundation. Twenty works, eleven artists, running 31 May to 18 October at plac Dąbrowskiego 8/11. Gierowski's canvases are distributed through the rooms as gravitational centres rather than historical anchors: a 1975 geometric painting set against Esther Mahlangu's Ndebele fields, late oils against Mona Hatoum's marbles, Andile Dyalvane and Zizipho Poswa's clay in the same argument as Olafur Eliasson's light. The claim is not that abstraction was secretly African. It is that light was never anybody's property. An estate letting an outside curator rewrite it is rarer than any single object in the room.

entries.name: Young M.A — KWEEN
entries.benchmark: Starlito
entries.read: Fifteen tracks, independent, 29 May, a decade after “OOOUUU.” The FADER got her on the record on 22 July and the interview is sharper than the album: a bottle a day, a 2023 hospitalisation for liver complications, and “Hennessy Medusa” as the one track where the writing catches the life. Sobriety is not a genre. The record made from the far side of it is the one worth waiting for.

issues.forecast: The sharpest account of the street economy published this year came from a legal scholar with footnotes, and two of the rappers on this board are narrating the same transaction from inside it. Capture over reform.
issues.climate: Capture over reform. Kojo Koram's question is who owns a criminalised economy once it goes legal, and the answer he finds across five continents is whoever already owned everything else. Read the rest of the board against that: two independent rappers building catalogues at a pace no label would fund, a self-taught artist in Los Angeles who took the most commodified cloth in America and treated it as a surface rather than a garment, and a two-person show in Sharjah paid for by the institution hanging it. Ownership is the only story here that is genuinely current.
come_up: Reportage over polemic — five continents, no thesis defended in advance
Commissioned over rented — Sharjah funding the work it hangs
The cloth as the surface, not the logo — denim artistry out of Los Angeles
decline: Release cadence as a substitute for a record
Shock titling as a growth strategy
Legalisation read as justice

entries.name: Kojo Koram — The Next Fix
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club
entries.read: Angola, Louisiana: a plantation that became a prison, and the first stop on a reporting trip that ends with Silicon Valley selling psilocybin as a wellness category. Koram crossed five continents to ask one question, and it is a property question rather than a moral one. When a criminalised substance is rebranded as a commodity, who is standing there to collect? Verso put the American edition out on 28 July, 304 pages, $29.95; John Murray had it in Britain on 4 June. He is a legal scholar, born in Accra and raised on Merseyside, and his first book, Uncommon Wealth, took the English PEN Hessell-Tiltman Prize and an Orwell shortlist for arguing that Britain's post-imperial economy was built by lawyers more than by statesmen. Same method here. Dispensaries now sell the thing that carried life sentences, and the sentences have not been unwound. He refuses the easy version and says so on the jacket: not a polemic for or against legalisation. Note what it isn't: a reform story with an ending. Akala calls the case irrefutable. Koram has worked the podcast circuit all month, This Is Hell! on 28 July, which is most of the reason a Verso title is moving at all.

entries.name: Body Quotidian — Laila Majid & Inaam Zafar
entries.benchmark: The Shed
entries.read: A misted bathroom mirror, UV-printed, that only completes itself once you stand in front of it. That is Laila Majid's Steam 07, 2026, and it hangs in Gallery 6 at Al Mureijah Square until 20 September beside Inaam Zafar's Mourners. Majid works out of London and shows with Niru Ratnam; Zafar works out of Lahore and shows with Grey Noise. Raja'a Khalid, an assistant curator, put the two of them in one room and let the proximity carry the argument: latex partitions and cat-toy tinsel on one wall, figuration dissolving into grief on the other. Sharjah commissioned Zafar's pieces rather than borrowing them, and entry costs nothing. That ordering matters.

entries.name: Janett Kabeh
entries.benchmark: Denim Tears
entries.read: Denim is the most over-explained cloth in America and the least often treated as a surface. Kabeh, self-taught, based in Los Angeles, came out of fashion design and went sideways into it: stitch as mark-making, pointillism in indigo, silhouettes built from hues of blue rather than printed onto them. She describes the subject as human touch and nostalgic eras, which reads soft until you notice she is making pictures out of the fabric itself rather than pictures on it. The public record is thin, and that is the honest part of this number: an Artsy listing, no dated survey, no institution behind her yet. Downtown Los Angeles opened an 11,000 square-foot Denim Institute Museum in June to enshrine 25 brands. The more interesting work is a few miles away, one person and a needle.

entries.name: Meechi Mono — Whoever Listens
entries.benchmark: Showly
entries.read: 63,719 monthly listeners, one album deep. Broward County, and the register is the post-Gen-Z one: melodic, aggrieved, closer to confession than to flex. Debut single Blocklist landed 11 July last year; The Viewing has done 614,000 plays with no press cycle behind it. Whoever Listens is the first full statement, and Rita followed it. Early, unproven, moving on its own steam.

entries.name: King Hendrick$ — Mob America 2
entries.benchmark: Chris Crack
entries.read: Leaving the Lot has 43.4 million plays and earns them; the man can build a hook that sounds like a parking lot at two in the morning. There is real lineage here too. Building Castles on Black Sand got a ChopNotSlop edition this year, which places him inside the DJ Screw succession rather than next to it, and that is a craft decision most rappers at 364,000 monthly listeners would not bother to make. The problem is the count. Eight projects across 2024 and 2025, then Mob America 2 and Rari Pedal this year, is a supply schedule rather than a discography, and a song titled Anne Frank is reach dressed as edge. The screw remix proves he knows what a record is. Nothing else on the release calendar behaves like it.

issues.forecast: A reed that Senegalese farmers pay to clear out of the river is now the insulation in Dakar's best new walls, and almost everything strong on this board was built from something already lying around. Reclamation over import.
issues.climate: Reclamation over import. Worofila's answer to a concrete city is a weed nobody wanted and soil dug from the site; Shannon Sanders' answer to the American family novel is a deed and four dead relatives who will not stop talking; DJ Doggo's answer to the UK garage revival is to produce it in Lisbon and press it in Rio rather than shipping it back to London. Read the counter-read the same way. Locarno is showing thirteen African films and 233 films in total, and that ratio is the festival's actual position on the continent, whatever the press release says. What looks weak this week is anything that had to be bought in.
come_up: Compressed earth and typha written as a spec, not a gesture
Catalogue numbers over rollouts: Lisbon produces, Rio presses
The ancestor as narrator and the deed as the plot
decline: The regional strand standing in for a programme
Concrete's borrowed prestige
Earth building filed under nostalgia

entries.name: Worofila
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey — an argument made in the material of the place, at building scale
entries.read: Typha is a cattail that has choked the Senegal River valley for decades, a green tide farmers pay to clear. Worofila weaves it into wall panels, lays it into ceiling mats and mixes it into adobe, because the stem is honeycombed with air and insulates better than most of what gets imported. The Dakar practice, founded in 2019 by Nzinga B. Mboup and Nicolas Rondet and named for the Fann-Hock street where its office sits, builds in compressed earth blocks in a city that wears a concrete skin. Facades step out in fine horizontal ridges so each course throws a blade of shade onto the one below it: the building cools itself with geometry and nothing else. The portfolio is not boutique. Houses at Sendou and Ngor, sixteen stations on Dakar's regional rail line, an eco-pavilion for the environment ministry, and the earth work on Kéré's Goethe-Institut Dakar, which opened 18 April. Mboup trained in Pretoria, passed through Adjaye Associates, and co-authored two studies of how Dakar actually houses itself. Next comes a gallery in Benin City raised in the Benin Kingdom's cob technique and a training centre at Sebikotane, so the method leaves the studio. That ordering matters.

entries.name: The Great Wherever — Shannon Sanders
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — the same insistence that the reading is about land, money and who kept the receipts
entries.read: Four ghosts narrate the parts of the story the living have agreed to forget. Sanders' first novel, out 7 July on Henry Holt at 416 pages, turns on a deed: a Tennessee farm bought by Thomas Lamb, one of the first Black landowners in his community, inherited a century later by a thirty-two-year-old gig worker in Washington with debt to clear. The room caught this one correctly. Starred reviews at Kirkus, Publishers Weekly and Booklist, a Book of the Month pick, summer lists at NPR, Esquire and People. What earns it is the voice rather than the premise. The dead are petty, funny and specific, passing judgment on romantic and sartorial decisions alike, which is exactly what keeps an inheritance saga from setting into a thesis.

entries.name: DJ Doggo — Ésselou / Latido Ao Luar
entries.benchmark: Jim Legxacy — the same splice instinct, minus the songs; Doggo works instrumental and lets the drum carry the argument
entries.read: Two tracks, catalogue 40FM096, out 12 November 2025 on the Rio label 40% Foda/Maneiríssimo. Diogo Vasconcelos produces from Lisbon and presses in Brazil, which is the whole idea: the garage shuffle travels south, the funk drum comes back north, and neither end is the guest. Bandcamp's 23 July scene report finally put the axis on the record. Almost nobody outside it has looked yet.

entries.name: Open Doors Screenings 2026 — Locarno
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive — which does the same curatorial work permanently, without needing a host festival's calendar
entries.read: The strand itself is genuinely programmed, which is what makes the arithmetic sting. Delphine Jeanneret and Ibee Ndaw have assembled thirteen films from twelve African countries for Locarno's 79th edition, 5 to 15 August, mixing fiction, documentary and hybrid work and asking to be sat with rather than sampled; the world premiere of Aymar Esse's La kora de mon père and the Swiss premiere of Ique Langa's The Prophet are in it. Then the numbers. Locarno is running 233 films from 69 countries with 103 world premieres, and the Piazza Grande belongs to Olivia Wilde and James Gray. A continent-wide focus that fits inside a sidebar is a focus a festival can quietly drop next August.

entries.name: Chapter 3 — Vanessa Lee
entries.benchmark: LAAMS — a small room that functions as infrastructure for a neighbourhood rather than a destination for visitors
entries.read: 4512 Third Street, Bayview, between La Salle Avenue and Third. Vanessa Lee, who already runs Smoke Soul Kitchen, has filed to open Chapter 3 there: a bookstore and cafe in a district that has spent years with the Linda Brooks-Burton Library as its only dependable source of books. Lee went to school in the Fillmore, a five-minute walk from Marcus Books, and that lineage is not decoration. Chapter 3 is one of nine Bayview storefronts funded this year through the city's Storefront Opportunity Grants, arriving just after a Renaissance Entrepreneurship Center and Harvard Business School study of the Third Street corridor recommended precisely this. A permit is not a ribbon. Come back when the door opens.

issues.forecast: What failed this week failed politely. Nina Protocol spent five years telling independent artists they could own their distribution, moved fifty thousand dollars in total, and was folded into SoundCloud on 22 July with the rails left behind. Everything that held up on this board arrived with its teeth already out. Friction over finish.
issues.climate: Friction over finish. dälek have been making the same argument out of Newark since 1998 and the eighth album states it in forty minutes without a single soft edge; Taring Padi have been printing that argument onto banners out of Yogyakarta since 1998 and hung thirty years of them in a Fitzrovia townhouse this month; Michelle Santiago Cortés spent an essay establishing that research without a verification step is just taste with a bibliography attached. Read the bottom of the board the same way. A book with the sharpest subject in the room arrives wrapped in a healing-journey register, and a platform built on artist ownership got acquired for its writing rather than for its artists. The work that kept an edge on it is the work that survived contact.
come_up: Records that argue: Ipecac's only rap act, eight tracks, no soft landings
The archive as the asset — SoundCloud bought Nina's criticism, not its rails
Woodcut and cardboard as distribution: the workshops, not the wall labels
decline: Artist ownership pitched as a deck rather than built as a business
The healing frame bolted onto a structural argument
Research with the accountability step quietly removed

entries.name: dälek — Brilliance of a Falling Moon
entries.benchmark: Chris Crack — the nearest thing on the 50, though dälek predate the lane by two decades
entries.read: Track six is called I AM A MAN, which is the placard Memphis sanitation workers carried in 1968, and Will Brooks never explains the reference because the record assumes you already have it. Eight tracks, forty minutes, out 27 March on Ipecac as IPC295LP: the eighth dälek album and the leanest, cut at Deadverse Studios across 2024 and 2025, mastered by Alan Douches at West West Side. Brooks and Mike Mare build it from dust-caked breaks, Wu-era strings and a wall of guitar feedback that never resolves, and the title is lifted from Erik Larson's account of Berlin before the war. Two things make it the record of this board rather than a good noise-rap album. dälek have done this from Newark since 1998, which makes them the ancestor of a lane that mostly does not know it has one. And they remain the only hip-hop act on a roster built for noise rock, so the aggression here is structural rather than borrowed. A June vinyl variant ran to 300 worldwide. The gap is that a catalogue this deep is still priced like a curiosity.

entries.name: Michelle Santiago Cortés — The End of Research
entries.benchmark: Free Game — the same gatekeeping instinct, turned on the people who borrowed the word
entries.read: OpenAI now sells a half-zip with the word Research embroidered on it in cursive. Santiago Cortés puts that merch drop at the centre of an argument about what the word has come to mean: moodboards, to-be-read lists, TikToks inviting you to spend a research day with someone, a whole leisure economy that borrowed academia's prestige and left the verification behind. Published 24 July in ArtReview. The sharpest turn is on artists, who she places awkwardly close to the scene of the crime once the accountability question is raised, since art has no protocols for verifying anything. It ends where the argument should start: nothing worth calling research survives without a little friction.

entries.name: Taring Padi — Rakyat Pasti Menang
entries.benchmark: Lauren Halsey — community-authored work built to leave the gallery, here at protest scale
entries.read: 93 Mortimer Street, London W1W 7SS, Wednesday to Sunday, eleven until six, running to 22 November. Ibraaz has given its Majlis over to nearly thirty years of banners from a collective founded by art students in Yogyakarta in 1998, in the months after Suharto fell. The title translates as the people united will never be defeated, and the display rotates rather than sitting still, which is the correct way to hang objects built to be carried. The workshops are the actual programme: cardboard puppetry on 11 July, woodcut printing on 12 July, both taught by the collective, because the whole method is reproducible by design. Taring Padi left documenta fifteen in 2022 with more than a thousand puppets and a banner removed over antisemitic imagery, for which they apologised. A thirty-year archive is not a clean object, and hanging it as though it were would have been the cowardly version.

entries.name: Dr. Sarah L. Webb — Colorism
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club — nearest on the 50 by subject, and nothing like it in register
entries.read: Legacy Lit, 7 July, 256 pages, $18.99. Webb has run the Colorism Healing platform for years and the ground covered here is wider than the discourse allows: dating and pop culture, yes, but also access to education, work, social services and politics, across communities of colour and white communities alike. The subject is a blade. The packaging is a healing journey. Only one of those two things travels.

entries.name: Nina Protocol — The SoundCloud Migration
entries.benchmark: Untitled Stream — the closest thing on the 50 to what Nina was trying to be
entries.read: Nina said it would be profitable if it ever reached ten percent of Bandcamp's daily volume. Components ran the arithmetic in July: fifty thousand dollars spent on Nina across its entire five-year life, against a hundred and fifty-one million on Bandcamp in 2025 alone. The platform went dark on 15 July; SoundCloud announced the acquisition on 22 July, terms undisclosed. Read what actually changed hands. Not the Solana marketplace, not the Arweave storage, not the team: the editorial archive and the genre map, which is to say the writing. Nina's most valuable product turned out to be its criticism, and it took a shutdown and a sale to establish that. Migrating artists get a free subscription until December.

issues.forecast: Accra spent this month building the institution London keeps convening panels about. Manju Journal, nine years a magazine, filed a nonprofit arm on 7 July and put a two-day textile workshop on the calendar for 20 August; the fund follows in 2027. The same instinct runs the length of this board. A Detroit rapper releases sixteen tracks with one guest on them. A Los Angeles singer spends the film budget on the song nobody streamed. Ownership over placement.
issues.climate: Ownership over placement. Every entry here is holding onto a piece of the process that the industry standard says to outsource. Iman Europe financed a short film for the album cut with twenty-six thousand plays instead of the one with 1.6 million, which is a decision about what an album is for. BandGang Lonnie Bands put out a sixteen-track record with a single feature on it, in a scene where the guest list is the marketing plan. Richmond Orlando Mensah turned a publication into a funder rather than waiting for a Western foundation to notice Accra. Read the bottom of the board against that. Ian Woods still cuts every piece by hand with a blade, and the hand is now aimed at Olympic sportswear and the most photographed faces alive, which is the one place on this board where the method outruns the subject. The measure this week is not who got the placement. It is who kept the thing after the placement was over.
come_up: The deep cut as the single: filming the 26,000-play song, not the 1.6-million one
Publications filing as institutions — Manju's 7 July conversion is the template
One guest across sixteen tracks: the record that doesn't rent an audience
decline: Placement as a career: the feature verse that outstreams your own catalogue forty to one
A gatekept method pointed at the most reproduced images on earth
Press for the scene with no structure underneath it

entries.name: Iman Europe — Ego Death (The Official Short Film)
entries.benchmark: Baby Rose — nearest on the 50 by voice and independence, though Iman Europe owns the release apparatus outright
entries.read: Iman Europe has a song with 1.6 million Spotify plays. She spent the film budget on one with 26,634. Ego Death is track five on Chrysalis, out 19 September 2025 on Good Soil Productions: fifteen tracks, every one of them built with Kaelin Ellis, which makes it a record rather than a folder of singles. The short film went up on her YouTube in the last week of July; Stanisland wrote it up on the 29th. Her own framing is a question about who wins between the ego and the self, and the film answers it rather than decorating the track. Nothing in the streaming math recommends any of this, and she knows that math better than most: she ran artist relations at Sound.xyz before going independent. Doing it anyway is the argument that an album is a body of work, not a container for the one song that travelled. Come back in November and see whether the film moved the number.

entries.name: Djamel White — All Them Dogs
entries.benchmark: Noname Book Club is the nearest thing on the 50, and it isn't close; the 50 carries no literary-fiction lane at all
entries.read: John Murray, 26 March 2026, 240 pages, a six-way auction behind it. Tony Ward comes back to West Dublin after five years away, takes work under an enforcer called Flute Walsh, and finds the pull is not towards the job. White is 28, managed a tattoo shop, lives in Lucan where the book is set, and grew the novel out of a short story written in the first lockdown. The Booker longlisted it on 28 July from 163 submissions and he is the youngest name on the list. Note what carries it: not the plot, which is standard gangland, but the vernacular, handled with enough precision that the judges led on the dialogue rather than the violence.

entries.name: New Africa Cultural Initiative
entries.benchmark: Black Film Archive — the same move, one person's archive hardening into an institution
entries.read: Manju Journal spent nine years documenting Ghanaian and pan-African creative work. On 7 July it filed a nonprofit arm and started programming instead. First cohort: 20 and 21 August in Accra at the Foundation for Contemporary Art, Zohra Opoku leading on textiles and archival photography, her first time running one. Lagos in October, Dakar in November, Abidjan in December. The unrestricted fund is promised for 2027, which is the part to check.

entries.name: BandGang Lonnie Bands — Motor City Slicker
entries.benchmark: Starlito — the same independent arithmetic, run over a decade and a half
entries.read: Sixteen tracks, forty-two minutes, one feature. KEY! turns up on Super Fancy and nobody else turns up at all, which on a 2026 Detroit rap album is close to a policy statement. Out 29 April on Antimedia and Roundvalley through Create Music Group. Delante Landrum has been doing this since he was thirteen, when BandGang formed around Six Mile Bronx on the west side, and the titles still read like a ledger: Det Blues, Detroit River pt 2, Charge It To The Game, Skeechy Lil Artist. The gap is in the streaming column. His biggest song by a distance is Homicide, where he is a guest on somebody else's record, at nearly 25 million plays; the cuts on this album sit in the low thousands. The catalogue he owns is the one nobody counts.

entries.name: Ian Woods
entries.benchmark: Robert Gallardo — the exact neighbour: Instagram-built, collage-rooted, working the seam between art and commerce
entries.read: The method has not changed since 2020 and the method is the whole argument: two printed images stacked, a pattern drawn on the top sheet, an X-Acto blade through both, glue, and a face that reads as two faces at once. Illinois born, Dallas raised, working out of Palm Bay. The New York Times Book Review put his jacket for Elias Canetti's I Want to Keep Smashing Myself Until I Am Whole, designed by Alex Merto at Picador, among the best covers of 2022. His project list now opens with Nike's Winter Olympics, Neymar's PUMA Future 9s, Shinola and the Jordan AJ40. The blade is gatekept. What it cuts is the most reproduced imagery on earth, and that is where the score settles.

issues.forecast: The only finished object on this board is a dress. Everything else is advance work: 106 seconds ahead of an album called Starlife, sixteen compiled tracks ahead of a debut called OSSHLAND, one viral record ahead of a catalogue, a browser beta at 69 pounds ahead of a plugin due in the fourth quarter. Finished small over promised large.
issues.climate: Finished small over promised large. Four of these five are advance work for something that has not shipped, so the read is which fragment stands up alone. Surf7's GOOSE COAT has 3.09 million Spotify plays and his next-biggest song has 252,000, which is a hit rather than a catalogue. Victony issued SLICK on his own OUTLAWVILLE imprint, licensed out rather than signed away, and then filled it with 106 seconds. Black Fortune spent nine months building Osshland into a vocabulary his audience actually speaks and still has not released the album it points at. Tim Exile discontinued one modular system in April and sold version 0.1 of its replacement in July, with the usable build promised for the fourth quarter. Against all of that, an Accra atelier cut a whole collection out of mill offcuts and hung it on a rail. It can be bought, worn and judged today, which this week is the rarer achievement.
come_up: Mill deadstock cut as the good cloth rather than the compromise
Own-imprint releases: licensing distribution out instead of signing yourself in
Builders leaving the big host to own their own stack
decline: The 106-second single working as an album announcement
One song at 3.09 million plays and the catalogue at a twelfth of it
Version 0.1 sold at full intent while the finished build waits on a quarter

entries.name: Ajepomaa Gallery — AHABAN
entries.benchmark: diasporic-fashion lane, nearest is Derschutze; the material discipline runs closer to Tamera
entries.read: The cloth starts as mill offcuts. AHABAN, named for the Akan word for leaf and built around what is left of Ghana's forests and waterways, is cut from handwoven Aso Oke and Fugu alongside cotton batik made from deadstock sourced out of GTP's mills, which puts the collection's material story in a warehouse most designers write off. The convention in luxury is to treat deadstock as a limitation and say so in the press release. Ajepomaa Mensah treats it as the good cloth and spends the hours on construction instead: knife, box, bias and sunburst pleats, origami folds worked into a batik that was never engineered to hold a shape. She has run the house out of Accra since February 2010 and sells it from 53 Adjiringano Road, from ₵1,288 for the Kenya top to ₵3,888 for the Halima dress, shipping free inside Ghana. Sixteen years in one city, no runway theatrics, and a rail of finished garments you can buy this afternoon.

entries.name: Victony — SLICK
entries.benchmark: already on the 50 in the global-diaspora lane; the honest test inside it is Baby Rose
entries.read: One minute forty-six seconds. SLICK landed on 8 July with the phonogram line reading OUTLAWVILLE, Victony's own imprint, and Encore holding the licence, which is a more interesting sentence than the song: at twenty-five, four years after Soweto made him portable, he is renting distribution rather than being absorbed by it. Ozedikus and Dera The Boy build the track from electronic texture over loose live percussion and leave the voice on top with nothing to fight. An influencer, Amma, opens it. It is well made and it is thin, a mood sustained for the length of a lift ride, and its job is to keep Starlife warm next to FRE$H. He is already in the 50. This is not the record that tests the seat.

entries.name: Black Fortune — Road To Osshland: The Series
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane, nearest in method is Chris Crack, who built a country out of a catalogue with no major behind him
entries.read: Osshland was a vocabulary before it was a place. Black Fortune, out of Landover, Maryland, has been extending the OSSH lexicon since OsshWop in 2018, through a near-fatal stabbing and the record he made after it, and on 8 May he compiled the four Road To Osshland EPs into a sixteen-track set with an interactive world attached. The guest list is loud: Denzel Curry, BIA, SleazyWorld Go, Doe Boy, Babyfxce E, Baby Kia. But the world is the achievement and the records read as evidence for it, which is the wrong way round. OSSHLAND, the debut all sixteen tracks point at, is still unreleased.

entries.name: Karst — Tim Exile
entries.benchmark: creator-ai-tools lane, nearest is Koala Sampler, which shipped small and then stayed shipped
entries.read: In April he shipped a modular system built on Reaktor. On 28 July he discontinued it and sold its replacement. Karst is Tim Exile leaving Native Instruments entirely: a node-based environment that autoconnects without cables, gives every instrument a generative DNA that passes clocks and triggers downstream, and folds composition and performance into the patching rather than treating them as the next step. He made the backers whole, which matters. What they got for it is version 0.1, browser-only, cloud-saved, at £69 against a £99 list, with the standalone and the plugin promised for the fourth quarter and new instruments arriving weekly. The instinct is right and the ledger is thin: two systems in four months, one of them already retired.

entries.name: Surf7 — GOOSE COAT
entries.benchmark: underground-rap lane, nearest is Showly; the difference is an audience built one release at a time
entries.read: Philadelphia decided this one. GOOSE COAT, self-released on 4 June with Surf7 holding both the copyright and the phonogram, has 3.09 million Spotify plays; his next-best song has 252,000. Meek Mill came for the remix on 24 July over a Beatsbyjxckk beat, and that version sits at 161,000. A city legend cosigning a hit is not the same thing as a second record.
